title.value: Memory-Aware Functional IR for Higher-Level Synthesis of Accelerators
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Memory-Aware Functional IR for Higher-Level Synthesis of Accelerators

extractions.description: This paper introduces Shir, a multi-level Intermediate Representation (IR) that exposes lower-level architectural features explicitly for generating high-performance hardware accelerators on FPGAs. The key contribution is the explicit handling of memory operations, including asynchronous off-chip memories and synchronous on-chip buffers, enabling the generation of hardware that can run on real FPGAs. The approach is evaluated on stencil computations and matrix multiplication, demonstrating competitive performance with OpenCL implementations.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on hardware acceleration and compiler optimization, not directly on sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This article adopts functional programming concepts to provide a hardware-agnostic higher-level pro- gramming abstraction. During synthesis, these abstractions are mechanically lowered into a functional IR (Intermediate Representation) that defines a specific hardware design point.

primary_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on hardware architecture and compiler optimization, rather than any specific Sustainable Development Goal.
primary_category.quote: Specialized accelerators deliver orders of a magnitude of higher performance than general-purpose processors. The ever-changing nature of modern workloads is pushing the adoption of FPGAs (Field Programmable Gate Arrays) as the substrate of choice. However, FPGAs are hard to program directly using HDLs (Hard- ware Description Languages).
